Your keyboard runs the Mac.

One key for every shortcut you set, and windows that tile, change layout and move between nine workspaces.

Hyper keys and binds

Caps Lock becomes Hyper. Hold it to see every key's job, then click a key on the board to give it a new one.

All 26 on the Binds page→

Tiling, layouts and workspaces

Windows tile as they open. Click the shown workspace in the top bar to cycle its layout, move and resize from the keyboard, and jump between nine workspaces.

Pilot, in use.

The tools you would otherwise buy or install, each used for a few seconds as you would use it.

Captures

Drag over an area and mark it up: arrows, steps, blur, a backdrop. Uncrop onto a backdrop, record the screen and cut the recording in its editor.

⇪SAll 29 on the Captures page→

Clipboard and notes

Hyper+V: everything you copied, sorted by kind, the words in your screenshots searchable. Quick notes a key away, and snippets that expand as you type.

⇪VAll 9 on the Clipboard page→

Update and Clean

Hyper+Space, update: every upgrade from every source, version to version, run when you press Return. Clean shows what it can free, then asks.

All 14 on the Update & Clean page→

Files

Hyper+F opens Pilot Files: folder sizes, ⌘K on every file and undo for every action. Find any file even with a typo, and convert one with a right-click.

All 3 on the File search page→

AI and dictation

Hyper+Q asks AI on the Claude or ChatGPT plan you already pay for and fixes text you select. Hold Right Control and talk: your words type as you speak, on your Mac.

⇪QAll 8 on the AI page→

Pilot
Pilot→dragApplications

Drag Pilot to Applications. Then hold Hyper.

Install Pilot 1.3.0.

Free and open source. Needs macOS 27 or later on Apple silicon.

  1. 1DownloadDrag Pilot to Applications
  2. 2Open PilotClick Open when macOS asks, once
  3. 3Pick your Hyper keyAnd allow Accessibility
Details
  1. Download Pilot.dmg, open it and drag Pilot to Applications.
  2. Open Pilot. macOS asks once whether to open an app downloaded from the Internet: click Open.
  3. Pick your Hyper key in Pilot's setup and allow Accessibility. Hyper+Space opens the menu.

Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. Updates install from inside Pilot.

Permissions and checking the download

  • Accessibility: Pilot needs it to see your keys and move windows; nothing works without it.
  • Full Disk Access for file search in the menu, and System Events for sleep, restart and dark mode.
  • Microphone for dictation and an AI provider for the AI chat, both optional.
  • Input Monitoring only if Pilot asks, when you bind a mouse's media buttons.
  • Screen Recording when you first take a screenshot or recording, or turn on Menu bar › Other apps › Show exact menu bar items. macOS applies it after Pilot reopens: click Quit & Reopen.

Caps Lock as Hyper: tapped alone it is Escape, and Shift+Caps Lock still types capitals. Password fields are blind to every key tap on macOS, Pilot's included: your binds do not work while one has focus.

Updates keep the permissions you gave. Check the download against the .sha256 beside it on the Releases page: shasum -a 256 -c Pilot.dmg.sha256.
